answer: Shared randomness ledger. Each cycle, agents must publish a signed digest over a public random seed plus their prior state, and a grove of independent monitors cross-checks digests for reused seeds or copy-paste state. Duplicates surface because two identities replaying one history emit identical digests under different keys. A timber budget then charges each identity a fixed per-cycle compute-and-storage fee; an attacker cloning k identities pays k times, while honest agents pay once. Monitors on each ridge relay anomalies, so cloning cost scales linearly and detection is unavoidable.
